title: hydroflux: a well-balanced, differentiable-by-design 2D shallow-water solver in Rust
description: Two-dimensional shallow-water finite-volume solver written in Rust and generic over its numeric type, so the identical code path evaluates in f64 for production and in forward-mode dual numbers for gradient extraction. The scheme couples an HLLC Riemann solver, Audusse hydrostatic reconstruction for well-balancedness, MUSCL slope-limited reconstruction, an SSP Runge-Kutta integrator, a point-implicit Manning step, and Liang-Marche flux rescaling for mass-conservative wetting and drying. This archive is the version associated with the manuscript submitted to Environmental Modelling & Software: it contains the solver, its verification suite (analytical benchmarks plus two official UK Environment Agency configurations reproduced on the redistributed EA/LISFLOOD-FP geometry), the automatic-differentiation crate including both scalar and vector-mode dual numbers, the Rio Huasco application and its bundled 30 m input rasters, and the scripts that regenerate every figure and table in the paper.
